doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24

title: Opening: date, names of Mr. and Mrs. Senegal and interviewers
summary: Dick Allen sets up the recording at 1938 Laperouse Street on May 24, 1962; the couple and interviewers give names, and Mrs. Senegal explains her family names.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Interview openings: names, dates and tape setup

blocks.x: Let's see, this is a real one of an interview. We're making it at 1938, is that right? 1938 Laferroose Street, and today is May the 20-something. 24th. May the 24th, 19...
1962. Let's get your names on here again.

Edna B. Senegal. Wait, I want my full name. This is Edna Bibelet Serena Senegal. That's my children's name, Serena. And I tell them about this tape. And Mother, you didn't put our name on there. You put an S. And it's Serena. Serena is the Spanish part of our family. So we should have Serena. This is my second marriage in Senegal. Our first marriage was to Serena. And he was the one that his grandfather came from Spain. So it's my children's grandfather. Great grandfather, see. And, uh, of course, French, came from my father. He's a peopleist. And my mother, I didn't say my mother's name, was Marceline LeBlanc. And I'm a mother. LeBlanc. Would you like Marceline? That's a pretty name. That's a beautiful name. Yeah, Marceline LeBlanc. That is my mother's name. Yeah. And, and... Okay, Marjorie Zander.
And I'm Dick Allen. I want to put our own names on here so that everybody will know what's what. Who's who. Who's who's going on. Who's who.
